faqs.question: What should I write in a Halloween card for my daughter?
faqs.answer: Write one line that names something only you noticed, such as the costume she built or the door she knocked on by herself. Under age 8, keep it to one breath so it can be read aloud; from about eight she will read it herself.

faqs.question: What is a good Halloween message for my son?
faqs.answer: End it with a question he can answer fast, like what he went as or his best sweet of the night. In a 2026 study of 99 US Muslim mothers, sons' conventional activities came to light mainly when mothers asked, while daughters volunteered more.

faqs.question: How do I wish my teenage daughter a happy Halloween without embarrassing her?
faqs.answer: Send a short private text or leave a note on her bed, and skip pet names and tags. Something like "Not posting this anywhere, you looked brilliant tonight" says it without an audience.

faqs.question: Should I post my teenager's Halloween costume photo on social media?
faqs.answer: Only after they say yes. In a Swedish survey of 68 children aged 4 to 17, parents posting pictures of them or writing about them on social media drew the most negative reactions, so ask first and keep a no as a no.

faqs.question: What do I text my child at college on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Send a short text on the night and save the longer chat for a weekend call. In one US study, first-year students exchanged a mean of 6.50 texts a day with their mother and 3.90 with their father, so one more short message fits the rhythm.

faqs.question: How do I wish my grown-up son a happy Halloween when he lives far away?
faqs.answer: Ring him, then follow up with a line that recalls a family Halloween. A 2026 analysis of 23 European countries found phone calls and visits remain the backbone of contact between older parents and adult children, with frequent video calls still rare.

faqs.question: What can a step-parent write to a stepdaughter or stepson for Halloween?
faqs.answer: Welcome them without claiming a role: offer a seat, a bowl of sweets or a shared joke, and leave the other household room. Avoid asking them to call you anything, and keep it to one or two sentences.

faqs.question: What date is Halloween in 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is always 31 October, which falls on a Sunday in 2027 and a Saturday in 2026. All Saints' Day follows on 1 November.

faqs.question: Can I send my daughter a Halloween card with our photos and music?
faqs.answer: Yes. SubhSandesh's /happy-halloween page takes up to six photos, a letter and a word to carve on a pumpkin, plus a YouTube link or one of eight Halloween favourites. Family mode changes the closing question to "Will you be my favourite little pumpkin?".

faqs.question: Is the SubhSandesh Halloween page suitable for a young child?
faqs.answer: Its Kids tone is spooky-cute: round blushing ghosts, no blood, gore or jump scares, and the trick becomes confetti spiders. The No button waits as "maybe later?", reduced motion is respected, and the interface is English only.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Wishes for Daughter or Son, From Age 3 to Grown-Up

Halloween wishes for daughter or son work best when they fit the child's stage: a silly line at five, a private text at fifteen, a call at thirty. Below are 57 original lines from a parent to their own child, sorted by stage and split into daughter, son and either.

Two SubhSandesh numbers, site-wide because we hold no Halloween data, shape the advice. On our pages, 48.3% of shared pages get opened on a phone, so keep lines short. And 38.5% of creators lock a page with a password before sending: senders value privacy, as teenagers do.

## What makes a parent's Halloween wish to their own child different?

A parent's Halloween wish comes from the one adult who remembers every costume, across years of 31 Octobers.

They confide in that adult. In a 2026 study of 12 Dutch adolescents aged 15 to 21, [participants disclosed most to caregivers, especially mothers](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13044866), and named privacy concerns as a barrier (Kullberg et al.).

## Halloween wishes for daughter and son, ages 3 to 12: 18 lines

Under-eights hear these read aloud, so keep each to one breath. From about eight, children read notes themselves.

### Little ones, ages 3 to 7

- **Daughter:** "Happy Halloween, my little witch. Broom parked, bedtime still counts."
- **Daughter:** "Bravest fairy on our street: you knocked on every door yourself, and I saw."
- **Daughter:** "Your pumpkin has a crooked grin, just like yours when you're plotting. Love, Mum."
- **Son:** "Happy Halloween, little dinosaur. Roar at every door, then say your thank-yous."
- **Son:** "Last year the big spider scared you. This year you named it Gary."
- **Son:** "To my small skeleton: your bones rattle and my heart does too when you laugh."
- **Either:** "Three knocks, one huge grin and a bucket nearly as heavy as you."
- **Either:** "Monsters are welcome here tonight, as long as they brush their fangs."
- **Either:** "Thanks for holding my hand on the dark bit of road."

### Tweens, ages 8 to 12

- **Daughter:** "You built that costume from a bin bag and an old hat. I'd hire you."
- **Daughter:** "Lead the group tonight; one text from the corner shop. Deal?"
- **Daughter:** "You still save the mint ones for me. That's a good heart in a ghoul suit."
- **Son:** "You traded every toffee for the flavour I like. I noticed."
- **Son:** "Your zombie shuffle is frankly worrying. Keep practising, champ."
- **Son:** "Home by eight, phone charged, one peanut-butter cup saved for your old man."
- **Either:** "Too tall for my old cape now, never too tall for a hug at the door."
- **Either:** "Whoever you dress up as tonight, I like the kid underneath best."
- **Either:** "Usual swap rules: you keep the chocolate, I take the raisin boxes."

## Halloween wishes for a teenage daughter or son, kept private: 9 lines

Teen lines work as a text or a note on the bed, never a tagged post. Skip pet names their friends might see.

- **Daughter:** "Not posting this anywhere. Just: you looked brilliant tonight."
- **Daughter:** "Saw the eyeliner work. Professional. Text when you're heading home."
- **Daughter:** "No photo needed for my wall; I'll remember tonight anyway. Love, Dad."
- **Son:** "Lifts home on offer until midnight, zero questions about the fake blood."
- **Son:** "That costume took you four hours and it shows. Respect."
- **Son:** "Pizza in the fridge if you beat your sister home."
- **Either:** "One text, then I'll leave you in peace: proud of you, enjoy it."
- **Either:** "Party dull? Text 'pumpkin' and I'll come and get you."
- **Either:** "I won't ask for a picture. I'd love one, privately, if you ever feel like it."

### When your teen doesn't want a public post

Ask before you post, even a costume photo. When Swedish researchers asked 68 children aged 4 to 17 about "sharenting", [they were most negative about parents posting pictures of or writing about them on social media](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10640438), and about photos taken without permission (Sarkadi et al., 2023).

That account summarises their paywalled 2020 study. Parents in the Kullberg study felt the tension too: approach the teen, or give them space?

## Halloween wishes for a grown daughter or son: 18 lines

Once a child leaves home, the wish is contact. Among 287 US first-year students a month into college, [students swapped a mean of 6.50 texts a day with their mother and 3.90 with their father](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11225983) (Morgan et al., 2024).

Later, calls matter more. Across 23 European countries, [face-to-face meetings and phone calls remain the backbone of contact between older parents and adult children](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13476080), while frequent video calls stay rare (Arpino et al., 2026).

### At college or away from home

- **Daughter:** "First Halloween without you on the porch. I left the light on anyway."
- **Daughter:** "A box of sweets is heading to your halls. Share them or hide them."
- **Son:** "Your brother wore your old vampire cape tonight. Still too big. Miss you."
- **Son:** "Please eat something that didn't come out of a vending machine."
- **Either:** "The dog barked at every trick-or-treater, then looked for you. So did I."
- **Either:** "Call on Sunday and tell me what you went as. I'll pretend I recognised it."

### Grown up and living far away

- **Daughter:** "Your homemade cat ears remain this family's finest costume."
- **Daughter:** "Your height marks are still on the kitchen door. I checked them tonight."
- **Son:** "Carved a pumpkin alone. It looks like your old maths teacher. You'd have laughed."
- **Son:** "Ring me after your first trick-or-treaters. Full report, please."
- **Either:** "Different time zone, same night: candle in the window at seven, your time."
- **Either:** "Spare key, spare sweets, same drawer as always."

### With children of their own

- **Daughter:** "Zipping your little one into a dragon suit? I zipped you into yours."
- **Daughter:** "You're on sweet-bag duty now. Welcome to the night shift, love."
- **Son:** "Your boys look exactly like you at that age, only with better costumes."
- **Son:** "Now you know why I always 'tested' your sweets first. Collect your toll."
- **Either:** "Send me one photo of the grandkids and one of you. The second matters too."
- **Either:** "You're the grown-up at the door now. I still see the little one who hid behind me."

## Halloween wishes for a stepdaughter or stepson: 6 lines

A step-parent's wish should welcome, never claim. These six lines leave room for the other household.

- **Daughter:** "I missed your first Halloweens, but I'm so glad I get this one."
- **Daughter:** "Your mum's house does the pumpkins; I do the hot chocolate. Come find me after."
- **Son:** "No pressure to call me anything. There's a seat for you here."
- **Son:** "You picked the scariest film and I covered my eyes first. Fair win."
- **Either:** "Two houses, double the sweets. I hope this porch feels like yours too."
- **Either:** "I'm not replacing anyone. I just wanted you to have a note from me."

## Halloween wishes for son: why a question gets an answer

A son may need asking before he tells you anything. In a 2026 study of 99 Muslim mothers in the United States, [mothers learned about sons' conventional activities mainly by asking, and about daughters' mainly from what daughters volunteered](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13643662) (Daddis et al.). The sample is specific, though wider Western studies also find girls disclose more. So end a son's wish with an easy question:

- "Happy Halloween, son. What did you end up going as?"
- "Best sweet of the night: go. I'll guess first. Toffee?"
- "Did the haunted house actually scare you, or was that for show?"
- "How many doors before you ran out of thank-yous?"
- "Which costume should I borrow next year, yours or your mate's?"
- "Out of ten, how scary was the party? Be honest."

## Which channel fits each stage of your child's life?

One daughter line, one son line and a channel for each stage. In 2027, 31 October is a Sunday.

| Child's stage | Daughter example | Son example | Channel |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ages 3 to 7 | "Bravest fairy on our street" | "Roar at every door" | Lunchbox note or bedtime card |
| Ages 8 to 12 | "I'd hire you" | "Keep practising, champ" | Note in the treat bag; one text |
| Ages 13 to 17 | "Not posting this anywhere" | "Lifts home on offer until midnight" | Private text, no tags |
| College or far away | "I left the light on anyway" | "Full report, please" | Text, then a weekend call |
| Grown with own kids | "Welcome to the night shift" | "Collect your toll" | Call, plus a link |

Small children need paper; older ones need privacy, then a call. A page holds several lines, and ours average 11.1 views each, so a family can replay one.

In Family mode, our [Halloween greeting page for one child](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) asks "Will you be my favourite little pumpkin?", and its Kids tone keeps ghosts round and cute, never gory. Your child knocks three times, carves a pumpkin until your chosen word lights up, and finds your letter in a dark attic; you can add as many as six photos.

For a grown child far away, the [premium version with your recorded voice](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) holds a voice note of up to a minute. In family and kids modes it has no No button.

## When a Halloween wish page is the wrong choice

A page cannot replace being there. Of the five stages, only the far-away ones need a link.

- **A child under 7 at home:** a lunchbox note beats any screen.
- **A teen who asked for no fuss:** send one line, not a page ending in a Story-sized Boo License.
- **A child who reads mainly another language:** the interface is English only.
- **A family party:** the page speaks to a single recipient, never a room.

## Sources

- Kullberg et al., [Adolescent self-disclosure across confidants](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13044866), *Journal of Adolescence*, 5 January 2026.
- Sarkadi et al., [Listening to children in research](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10640438), *Clin Child Fam Psychol Rev*, 12 September 2023.
- Morgan et al., [Parent-student texts and calls at college](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11225983), *Cannabis*, 26 June 2024.
- Arpino et al., [Parent-adult child contact across Europe](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13476080), *J Gerontol B*, 1 August 2026.
- Daddis et al., [Mothers, daughters and sons](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13643662), *Journal of Adolescence*, 31 July 2026.
- SubhSandesh first-party data, 24 September 2026.

sources.stat: Sarkadi et al., Clinical Child and Family Psychology Review (Springer, CC BY): summarising their 2020 study, children aged 4–17 (N = 68) answered an anonymous picture-supported questionnaire on sharenting and were most negative towards parents posting pictures of or writing about them on social media, and towards a photo taken without permission. Full text of the 2023 paper read; the 2020 original (J Paediatr Child Health, doi 10.1111/jpc.14945) is paywalled and was not read. Note: a 2025 review describes the same sample as aged 4–15.

Kullberg, Keijsers, Elzinga & Janssen, Journal of Adolescence (Wiley, CC BY): 12 Dutch adolescents (ages 15–21, mean 18.3) and their parents; adolescents disclosed most to caregivers, especially mothers, least to familiar adults such as teachers; barriers included emotional distance and privacy concerns; parents described a dilemma between approaching the child and giving space. Full text read.

Morgan, Trager, Boyle, Rainosek & LaBrie, Cannabis (CC BY-NC-ND, cited not reused): N = 287 US first-year students surveyed in October 2021, about a month into college; mean texts exchanged per day with mother 6.50 (SD 5.08), with father 3.90 (SD 4.07); calls 2.07 and 1.24. Only the descriptive figures are used; the study's aim was cannabis use. Full text read.

Arpino, Tosi & Bordone, Journals of Gerontology Series B (OUP, CC BY): SHARE wave 9 and ESS round 10 data for 23 European countries; face-to-face meetings and phone calls remain the backbone of older parent–adult child ties, text messaging is less widespread and frequent video calls relatively rare. Full text read.

Daddis, Metzger & Said, Journal of Adolescence (Wiley, CC BY-NC-ND, cited not reused): 99 Muslim mothers in the US of adolescents (mean age 13.87); for conventional issues, solicitation was the primary knowledge source for sons and voluntary disclosure for daughters; the authors note broader Western samples find girls disclose more. Full text read.

auditReport.honestAssessment: The five pages analysed (two near-identical wish farms, a generic kids list, Hallmark's card guide, a thin 2023 list) sort daughter lines by tone or sender; none covers adult children, a son's lines next to a daughter's at each stage, or a teen's objection to public posts, and none cites any research. This post is the only one with stage-by-stage daughter/son lines, five open-access studies and a channel table, but its first-party numbers are platform-wide, not Halloween-specific, and incumbents like Hallmark hold far more authority, so expect slow gains, not a quick ranking.
